meta.spec_reference: Multimedia Programming Interface and Data Specifications 1.0 (IBM and Microsoft, August 1991) for the RIFF container and the chunk envelope; the Microsoft AVI RIFF File Reference (AVIMAINHEADER, AVISTREAMHEADER, AVIINDEXENTRY and the 'hdrl', 'strl', 'movi' and 'idx1' chunk layout, and the ##db/##dc/##wb/##pc/##tx data chunk naming); Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER and RGBQUAD (wingdi.h) for the video stream's format chunk; Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX (mmreg.h) for the audio stream's format chunk; the OpenDML AVI File Format Extensions 1.02 (OpenDML AVI M-JPEG File Format Subcommittee, 1996) for the 'odml' list and the above-4 GB 'AVIX' form.

schema_extensions.name: comparison_sites
schema_extensions.why: The LIST form type is the sole dispatch for the whole body of the file, but unlike the top-level chunk identifier it is not decided by a lookahead - it is a field already read, compared three times by Memcmp at lines 179, 183 and 202. The `lookahead` key therefore cannot carry it, yet it is exactly the good-known-value set a mining pass needs. comparison_sites records each site with its line and the literal compared there.

schema_extensions.name: fixed_result / fixed_result_hex
schema_extensions.where: the avihHEADER.data, strhHEADER.data, strfHEADER_BIH.bmiHeader, strfHEADER_BIH.bmiColors, strfHEADER_WAVE.wave, LISTHEADER.avhi, LISTHEADER.strh, WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize, BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSize, BITMAPINFO.bmiHeader, BITMAPINFO.bmiColors and AVIStreamHeader.xdwQuality entries
schema_extensions.why: Each of these is typed calculated_value because it is a length or a derived region, yet each has a byte count or a value the specification fixes rather than a field: 56 for the main header, 64 for the stream header, 40 for a bitmap header, 18 for a WAVEFORMATEX, 4 for one RGBQUAD and 0 for a PCM cbSize. fixed_result records the constant so the rewrite step can emit it directly, while algorithm/covers/includes_self still document what the field measures.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout
schema_extensions.why: The 16-byte stride of an AVIINDEXENTRY is what turns the chunk size into an entry count - the template divides by the AVIINDEXENTRYLEN constant at line 250 - and the per-field breakdown is nowhere stated in the .bt outside the struct definition. The rewrite step needs both to convert between an entry count and the enclosing chunk size.

schema_extensions.name: unused_in_parse_flow
schema_extensions.why: BITMAPINFO is typedef'd at lines 71-75 but never instantiated - strfHEADER_BIH declares its own bmiHeader and bmiColors inline instead. The flag tells the rewrite step that these entries describe declared-but-dead code, so it may wire the struct up or skip it, but must not assume it is currently reachable.

schema_extensions.name: element-level key ROOT.id[3]
schema_extensions.where: the ROOT.id[3] entry alongside the whole-field ROOT.id entry
schema_extensions.why: The fourth signature byte carries a constraint the other three do not: the template tests it directly at line 257 to choose the file's byte order, making it the format's only endianness switch. The schema permits a STRUCT.field[i] key exactly when one array element is separately constrained, and this is that case - the whole-field entry gives the two legal four-character codes while the element entry gives the dispatch.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: This template validates only the 'AVI ' form type, and it disagrees with the specifications in fourteen concrete places: a movi loop whose exact-equality exit condition never terminates on overshoot, a header list whose stream children are never read as children, an unconditionally-required optional chunk, four unguarded length subtractions, a colour table detected by an exact size test, four reserved words named as timing fields, a RECT read as two DWORDs, two WORDs read as one, a dead struct, an ignored container size, a signature check that examines one byte of four, six chunks with no padding branch and three fixed-shape structures whose declared sizes are never honoured. A generator that imitated the parser's laxity would emit files this template accepts and no player does, so these must be visible as data rather than buried in prose.

schema_extensions.name: cross_chunk emphasis in generation_range rationales
schema_extensions.where: AVIINDEXENTRY.dwChunkOffset, AVIINDEXENTRY.dwChunkLength, ROOT.datalen, LISTHEADER.datalen and MainAVIHeader.dwStreams
schema_extensions.why: These fields are not merely bounded numbers - each must be back-patched from a measured layout or counted from elements generated elsewhere, and the index offsets carry the additional ambiguity that some writers measure them from the file start rather than from the movi list. The schema has no key for 'this must be computed after the fact', so the requirement is stated inside each rationale where a generator author will read it alongside the bound.

schema_extensions.name: note on the absent enum section

meta.structure_note: A RIFF container with NO terminator: a 12-byte 'RIFF' + size + 'AVI ' header followed by a flat stream of chunks, each a four-character identifier, a 32-bit little-endian size, that many data bytes and a pad byte when the size is odd - of which a 'hdrl' LIST carrying the main header and one 'strl' list per stream must come first, a 'movi' LIST carrying the frame and audio chunks must follow, and an optional 'idx1' index whose offsets are measured from the movi list must come last.

WAVEFORMATEX.wFormatTag.description: Audio format code for an 'auds' stream's format chunk; it decides whether the sample bytes are raw PCM or a compressed stream.

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX (mmreg.h) as used by the AVI 'strf' chunk of an 'auds' stream: 'wFormatTag - Waveform-audio format type. Format tags are registered with Microsoft Corporation for many compression algorithms.' WAVE_FORMAT_PCM is 1 and is the only tag for which the sample bytes need no valid compressed stream. The template reads a plain WORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.wFormatTag.notes: Byte order is chosen at parse time by the guard at lines 257-266: a fourth signature byte of 'X' (i.e. 'RIFX') switches the whole file to big-endian, anything else to little-endian. Every multi-byte field in the format follows that choice, and 'RIFF' - little-endian - is what every real AVI uses. The whole WAVEFORMATEX struct is 18 bytes, which is the constant the template subtracts at line 146 to size the trailing exData array.

WAVEFORMATEX.nChannels.description: Number of interleaved audio channels; it is one of the two factors of the block alignment.

generation_range.rationale: A channel count of 0 makes nBlockAlign zero, which is a division by zero in every duration computation a player performs. 1 (mono) and 2 (stereo) are what real files use, and the count multiplies into nBlockAlign and nAvgBytesPerSec, so all three must be chosen together.

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'nChannels - Number of channels in the waveform-audio data. Monaural data uses one channel and stereo data uses two channels.' A zero channel count is meaningless. The template reads a plain WORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.nSamplesPerSec.description: Sampling rate in sample frames per second; it must be non-zero and is one of the two factors of the average byte rate.

generation_range.rationale: Real rates are 8000, 11025, 22050, 44100 and 48000. A 32-bit value near four billion makes nAvgBytesPerSec - which must equal this times nBlockAlign - overflow its own 32-bit field, so the two cannot both be consistent at extreme values, and a rate of 0 is a division by zero in any duration computation.

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'nSamplesPerSec - Sample rate, in samples per second (hertz).' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec.description: Average data rate in bytes per second; for uncompressed PCM it is exactly the sampling rate times the block alignment.
WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec.algorithm: nSamplesPerSec * nBlockAlign for uncompressed formats; for a compressed format it is the encoder's average output rate
WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec.covers: nothing itself; it is a derived rate describing the audio stream's data

generation_range.rationale: Must equal nSamplesPerSec * nBlockAlign for PCM, so it is not free at all - the ceiling here is 48 kHz stereo 32-bit. Choosing it independently of the rate and block alignment is the most common way a generated audio format chunk becomes internally inconsistent, and the AVI main header's dwMaxBytesPerSec should be at least the sum of this across all streams.

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'nAvgBytesPerSec - Required average data-transfer rate, in bytes per second, for the format tag. Playback software can estimate the buffer size using the nAvgBytesPerSec member.' For WAVE_FORMAT_PCM it must equal nSamplesPerSec times nBlockAlign. The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign.description: Size in bytes of one complete sample frame across all channels; a player must process a whole multiple of it at a time.
WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign.algorithm: nChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 for uncompressed formats; for a compressed format it is the encoder's block size
WAVEFORMATEX.nBlockAlign.covers: nothing itself; it is the stride of one sample frame in the audio stream's data chunks

generation_range.rationale: Must equal nChannels * wBitsPerSample / 8 for PCM, giving 1 for 8-bit mono through 8 for 32-bit stereo. A value of 0 is a division by zero wherever a player converts bytes to frames, and it must also agree with the stream header's dwSampleSize for an audio stream.

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'nBlockAlign - Block alignment, in bytes. The block alignment is the minimum atomic unit of data for the wFormatTag format type. ... software must process a multiple of nBlockAlign bytes of data at a time.' For PCM it must equal nChannels times wBitsPerSample divided by 8. The template reads a plain WORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.wBitsPerSample.description: Bits in each individual sample of one channel; for PCM it must be a multiple of 8.
value_names: 0 - not applicable to this compressed format

evidence.note: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'wBitsPerSample - Bits per sample for the wFormatTag format type. If wFormatTag is WAVE_FORMAT_PCM, then wBitsPerSample should be equal to 8 or 16. ... If wFormatTag is any other format, this member must be set to some acceptable value, or 0 if it is not applicable.' The template reads a plain WORD and performs no check.

WAVEFORMATEX.wBitsPerSample.notes: Note the sign convention the format inherits from WAVE: 8-bit PCM samples are UNSIGNED with 128 as silence, while 16-bit and wider are SIGNED two's complement with 0 as silence.

WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize.description: Byte count of the format-specific extension following this structure; zero for plain PCM, and the template always reads the field whatever it says.
WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize.algorithm: byte count of the extension bytes after the 18-byte WAVEFORMATEX; it must equal the strf chunk's datalen minus 18
WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize.covers: the strfHEADER_WAVE.exData bytes that follow; it excludes the 18 bytes of WAVEFORMATEX itself

generation_range.rationale: 0 for WAVE_FORMAT_PCM and 22 for WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE are the only values in ordinary use. The template does NOT use this field to size anything - it computes exData as datalen - 18 at line 146 instead - so a cbSize that disagrees with that subtraction is invisible here and wrong for every real reader.

WAVEFORMATEX.cbSize.notes: Microsoft WAVEFORMATEX: 'cbSize - Size, in bytes, of extra format information appended to the end of the WAVEFORMATEX structure. This information can be used by non-PCM formats ... For the PCM format, this member is ignored.' TEMPLATE DEVIATION: a strict WAVEFORMAT (as opposed to WAVEFORMATEX) has no cbSize at all and is 16 bytes, so an AVI whose audio strf chunk is 16 bytes long makes the template read two bytes past the end of the chunk.

MainAVIHeader.dwMicroSecPerFrame.description: Frame period in microseconds; it is the reciprocal of the frame rate and must agree with the video stream's rate over scale.
MainAVIHeader.dwMicroSecPerFrame.algorithm: 1000000 / frame rate; equivalently 1000000 * AVIStreamHeader.dwScale / AVIStreamHeader.dwRate for the video stream
MainAVIHeader.dwMicroSecPerFrame.covers: nothing itself; it states the presentation interval of one frame

generation_range.rationale: 4166 microseconds is 240 frames per second and 1000000 is one frame per second; real files sit between 33367 (29.97 fps) and 40000 (25 fps). A value of 0 is a division by zero wherever a player computes a frame rate, and a 32-bit value describes a frame lasting over an hour.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwMicroSecPerFrame - Specifies the number of microseconds between frames. This value indicates the overall timing for the file.' It must be consistent with the video stream header's dwRate and dwScale. The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwMaxBytesPerSec.description: Approximate maximum data rate of the whole file; a player uses it to decide whether it can sustain playback.
MainAVIHeader.dwMaxBytesPerSec.algorithm: the sum across all streams of their average bytes per second, i.e. at least the sum of every WAVEFORMATEX.nAvgBytesPerSec plus the video stream's data rate
MainAVIHeader.dwMaxBytesPerSec.covers: nothing itself; it describes the file's aggregate data rate

generation_range.rationale: It costs no file bytes but a player may pre-allocate from it. 10 MB/s covers any generated file; 0 is tolerated by most readers as 'unknown'. It should be at least the sum of the per-stream rates or the file contradicts itself.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwMaxBytesPerSec - Specifies the approximate maximum data rate of the file. This value indicates the number of bytes per second the system must handle to present an AVI sequence as specified by the other parameters contained in the main header and stream header chunks.' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwReserved1.description: Padding granularity in modern documentation and a reserved field in the original AVI specification; either reading makes zero or 2048 the only sensible values.

evidence.note: The original AVI specification names this field dwReserved1 and requires it to be zero; Microsoft's later AVIMAINHEADER renames it dwPaddingGranularity and defines it as 'the alignment for data, in bytes. Pad the data to multiples of this value', for which the value is conventionally 2048 when JUNK padding is used and 0 otherwise. The template reads a plain DWORD, keeps the reserved name, and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwReserved1.notes: This is the only field in the AVI main header whose two published readings disagree; 0 is safe under both.

MainAVIHeader.dwFlags.description: Main header flags declaring whether the file has an index, is interleaved, and how a player may use them.
MainAVIHeader.dwFlags.valid_bits: 0x00000010 AVIF_HASINDEX - the file has an idx1 index; 0x00000020 AVIF_MUSTUSEINDEX - the index rather than the physical ordering defines the presentation order; 0x00000100 AVIF_ISINTERLEAVED - the streams are interleaved; 0x00000800 AVIF_TRUSTCKTYPE - the chunk type codes may be trusted; 0x00010000 AVIF_WASCAPTUREFILE; 0x00020000 AVIF_COPYRIGHTED. Every other bit is reserved and must be 0

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwFlags - Contains a bitwise combination of zero or more of the following flags: AVIF_COPYRIGHTED, AVIF_HASINDEX, AVIF_ISINTERLEAVED, AVIF_MUSTUSEINDEX, AVIF_WASCAPTUREFILE.' The AVIF_HASINDEX bit is a promise that an idx1 chunk exists, which is why it is a cross-section constraint rather than a free flag. The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwFlags.notes: valid_values lists the combinations a real file carries; the individual bits are in valid_bits and a real flags word is their OR.

MainAVIHeader.dwTotalFrames.description: Total number of frames of data in the file; it should equal the video stream header's dwLength.
MainAVIHeader.dwTotalFrames.algorithm: frame count of the file's video stream; it should equal the video AVIStreamHeader.dwLength and the number of '##dc' or '##db' chunks in the movi list
MainAVIHeader.dwTotalFrames.covers: nothing itself; it counts the frames the movi list holds

generation_range.rationale: Each frame is a whole chunk in the movi list with its own eight-byte header, so this count multiplies file size directly. A 32-bit frame count describes a file a player builds a seek bar for. It must equal the number of video chunks actually written, so it cannot be drawn independently.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwTotalFrames - Specifies the total number of frames of data in the file.' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwInitialFrames.description: Initial frame count for interleaved files; the specification requires zero for a non-interleaved file.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwInitialFrames - Specifies the initial frame for interleaved files. Noninterleaved files should specify zero. If you are creating interleaved files, specify the number of frames in the file prior to the initial frame of the AVI sequence in this member.' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwStreams.description: Number of streams in the file; it must equal the number of 'strl' lists inside the 'hdrl' list.
MainAVIHeader.dwStreams.algorithm: count of LIST chunks whose type is 'strl' inside the hdrl list
MainAVIHeader.dwStreams.covers: nothing itself; it counts the stream header lists that follow the main header

generation_range.rationale: Each stream costs a whole strl list containing a strh, a strf and a strn chunk, and the count must equal the number actually written. Real AVIs carry one video stream and optionally one audio stream; a 32-bit count promises billions of stream lists that the file does not contain.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwStreams - Specifies the number of streams in the file. For example, a file with audio and video has two streams.' The template reads a plain DWORD and never uses it to bound anything. A count that disagrees with the strl lists present is the most common way a hand-built AVI header contradicts its own body.

MainAVIHeader.dwSuggestedBufferSize.description: Suggested read-buffer size, large enough to hold the biggest chunk in the file; a player may pre-allocate exactly this much.
MainAVIHeader.dwSuggestedBufferSize.algorithm: the byte size of the largest chunk in the movi list, or of the largest record when the file is interleaved
MainAVIHeader.dwSuggestedBufferSize.covers: nothing itself; it advises a reader how much to buffer

generation_range.rationale: A player allocates this much on opening the file, so a 32-bit value asks for up to 4 GB from four header bytes - the classic AVI resource-exhaustion shape. 0 is legal and means the reader should work it out for itself, and it should otherwise equal the largest chunk actually written.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwSuggestedBufferSize - Specifies the suggested buffer size for reading the file. Generally, this size should be large enough to contain the largest chunk in the file. ... If the value is set to zero, or is too small, the playback software will have to reallocate memory during playback, which will reduce performance.' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwWidth.description: Width of the AVI file's presentation rectangle in pixels; it should equal the video stream's bitmap width.
MainAVIHeader.dwWidth.algorithm: pixel width of the presentation rectangle; it should equal BITMAPINFOHEADER.biWidth of the video stream's format chunk
MainAVIHeader.dwWidth.covers: nothing itself; it declares the frame geometry a player allocates for

generation_range.rationale: A player allocates dwWidth * dwHeight * bytes-per-pixel on reading the header, so the 32-bit range forces an absurd allocation from four header bytes. 1-640 keeps generated frames trivially cheap while still exercising the stride arithmetic, and it must agree with the bitmap header's biWidth.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwWidth - Specifies the width of the AVI file in pixels.' It should match the width in the video stream's BITMAPINFOHEADER. The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwHeight.description: Height of the AVI file's presentation rectangle in pixels; it should equal the video stream's bitmap height.
MainAVIHeader.dwHeight.algorithm: pixel height of the presentation rectangle; it should equal the absolute value of BITMAPINFOHEADER.biHeight of the video stream's format chunk
MainAVIHeader.dwHeight.covers: nothing itself; it declares the frame geometry a player allocates for

generation_range.rationale: Same frame-buffer allocation blow-up as dwWidth; the product of the two is what a player reserves, so both must be capped together. Note the bitmap header's biHeight may be negative to mean top-down while this field is always positive.

evidence.note: Microsoft AVIMAINHEADER: 'dwHeight - Specifies the height of the AVI file in pixels.' The template reads a plain DWORD and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwScale.description: The first of the four reserved words that end the AVI main header; Microsoft's AVIMAINHEADER requires all four to be zero.

evidence.note: Microsoft's AVIMAINHEADER ends with `DWORD dwReserved[4]` - four reserved words that must be set to zero. The template names them after the older AVI documentation's dwScale, dwRate, dwStart and dwLength, which is why they look like meaningful timing fields. They are not: in the MAIN header these four words are reserved, and only the STREAM header has real dwScale, dwRate, dwStart and dwLength fields. The template reads plain DWORDs and performs no check.

MainAVIHeader.dwScale.notes: These four are the AVI main header's only reserved fields besides dwReserved1, and the template's misleading names are the single most likely thing to make a generator write meaningful timing values where zeros belong.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSize.description: Size in bytes of the bitmap info header, counting itself; the template reads a fixed 40-byte layout whatever the field says.
BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSize.algorithm: byte count of the DIB header including this size field
BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSize.covers: the BITMAPINFOHEADER structure itself, from this field through biClrImportant; it excludes the colour table and the chunk header

generation_range.rationale: The template reads exactly the 40-byte layout at lines 48-61 and then computes `sizeof(bmiHeader)` into the local sz at line 129, so any other value desynchronises the exData subtraction at line 136. The BMP family defines other header sizes - 12, 52, 56, 64, 108, 124 - none of which this template can parse.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSize.notes: Declared at line 50. Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biSize - Specifies the number of bytes required by the structure.' A reader is expected to switch on it to choose the header layout.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biWidth.description: Width of the video frame in pixels; it should equal the main header's dwWidth.

generation_range.rationale: A decoder allocates biWidth * biHeight * biBitCount / 8 bytes on reading the format chunk, so the spec range forces an absurd allocation. It must also agree with MainAVIHeader.dwWidth, and the row stride is rounded up to a multiple of 4 bytes, which is where the interesting arithmetic lives.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biWidth - Specifies the width of the bitmap, in pixels.' A zero width describes an empty image. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared uint32 here where the BMP specification and Microsoft's own header define a signed LONG. The template performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biHeight.description: Height of the video frame in pixels, with its sign carrying meaning: positive is bottom-up and negative top-down.

generation_range.rationale: Same frame-buffer allocation blow-up as biWidth. TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared uint32 where the specification defines a signed LONG whose negative values mean top-down row order, so a top-down bitmap reads as a height near four billion here. A generator should keep it positive, which is the bottom-up default AVI uses.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biHeight - Specifies the height of the bitmap, in pixels. If biHeight is positive, the bitmap is a bottom-up DIB and its origin is the lower left corner. If biHeight is negative, the bitmap is a top-down DIB and its origin is the upper left corner.' The template reads an unsigned uint32 and performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biPlanes.description: Number of colour planes; the specification fixes it at 1 and no other value has ever been defined.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biPlanes - Specifies the number of planes for the target device. This value must be set to 1.' The template reads a plain uint16 and performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biBitCount.description: Bits per pixel of the video frames; it decides whether a colour table is present and how wide it is.
value_names: 0 - the bit count is defined by the codec (JPEG or PNG compression)

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biBitCount - Specifies the number of bits per pixel. This value must be 1, 4, 8, 16, 24, or 32.' In an AVI the value 0 is additionally used when the codec named by biCompression defines the pixel format itself. The template reads a plain uint16 and performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biBitCount.notes: For a palettised depth the format chunk should carry 2^biBitCount RGBQUAD entries after the header, which is the region the template's exData array at line 136 absorbs.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biCompression.description: Compression method, which in an AVI is usually a four-character codec code rather than one of the BMP numeric constants.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biCompression - Specifies the type of compression for a compressed bottom-up bitmap' - BI_RGB 0, BI_RLE8 1, BI_RLE4 2, BI_BITFIELDS 3. In a video stream's format chunk the field instead carries a FOURCC codec identifier registered with Microsoft, which is why the four-character values appear here as their little-endian numeric equivalents. The template reads a plain uint32 and performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biCompression.notes: BI_RGB (0) is strongly preferred for generation: it is the only value for which the frame bytes need no valid compressed stream, so a decoder reaches the pixel data rather than failing in a codec. It should also agree with the stream header's fccHandler.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSizeImage.description: Size in bytes of one uncompressed frame; it may be zero for BI_RGB bitmaps.
BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSizeImage.algorithm: for BI_RGB, biHeight * ((biWidth * biBitCount + 31) / 32) * 4, i.e. the row stride rounded up to a 4-byte boundary times the row count; for a compressed format it is the encoder's output size and may be 0
BITMAPINFOHEADER.biSizeImage.covers: nothing in the header itself; it states the byte size of one decoded frame

generation_range.rationale: It must equal the computed frame size for BI_RGB or be 0. A 32-bit value describes a frame larger than any generated file, and a decoder may allocate from it before reading a single pixel.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biSizeImage - Specifies the size, in bytes, of the image. This can be set to zero for BI_RGB bitmaps.' The template reads a plain uint32 and performs no check.

BITMAPINFOHEADER.biXPelsPerMeter.description: Horizontal resolution of the target device in pixels per metre; purely informational and commonly zero.

generation_range.rationale: Real values are 0 (unspecified) or around 2835, which is 72 dpi expressed in pixels per metre. Viewers multiply this into layout arithmetic, so values near the 32-bit ceiling produce absurd physical sizes without adding coverage.

evidence.note: Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER: 'biHPelsPerMeter - Specifies the horizontal resolution, in pixels per meter, of the target device for the bitmap.' TEMPLATE DEVIATION: declared uint32 where the specification defines a signed LONG. The template performs no check.

template_deviations.subject: the movi loop exits on exact equality and can never terminate on overshoot
template_deviations.issue: The do-while at lines 209-214 accumulates `sizeof(gb)` into the local pointer and exits on `while (pointer != stop)`, where stop is `datalen - 4`. There is no `<` comparison and no end-of-file guard.
template_deviations.impact: If the chunk sizes overshoot the list size by even one byte the pointer skips past stop and the loop runs forever, reading chunk after chunk off the end of the file. It is also a DO-while, so an empty movi list - datalen 4, stop 0 - still reads one chunk and can then never reach the equality. This is the template's most dangerous construct.
template_deviations.action: Make the sum of every chunk's padded size equal LISTHEADER.datalen - 4 exactly, and never emit an empty movi list.

template_deviations.subject: the header list's strl children are never read as children
template_deviations.issue: The hdrl branch at lines 179-182 reads exactly one avih chunk and then falls out of the LISTHEADER struct. The strl lists that the same hdrl list contains are left to the top-level loop, which picks them up as if they were siblings of the hdrl rather than its children.

The hdrl list's own declared size is never used to bound anything, so a hdrl whose size disagrees with its contents is never detected.
template_deviations.action: Lay the strl lists out immediately after the avih chunk inside the hdrl, and set the hdrl size to cover them.

template_deviations.subject: the strn chunk is read unconditionally

template_deviations.impact: A stream list without a strn - which is the common case - makes the template read the next chunk's header as a strn, and every byte after that is misaligned.
template_deviations.action: Always emit a strn chunk in every strl list.

template_deviations.subject: four unguarded length subtractions
